lawyer:
Shamsuddin Babul, Md Ib ahinr Khalil and Ms Bahasti Marjan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners. 
Md Mamunur Rashid, Assistant Attorney-General  ----- For the State.
parties:
Nurul Amin Chowdhury and another ----- Accused-Petitioner 
Vs.
State ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J: This Rule under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was issued on 25-8-2010 calling upon the opposite-party to show cause as to why the proceedings of the Motijheel police Station Case No. 89(10) 2002 corresponding to BAGR Case No. 100 of 2002 under sections 406/467/ 468/471 and 109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, now pending in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Dhaka should not be quashed and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, all further proceedings of the above mentioned Case was stayed for a period of 6(Six) months which has been further extended for 1 (one) year by order dated 15-2-2010. 

 5. The petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 surrendered before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka on 6-11-2003 and 10-8-2004 respectively and the learned Magistrate was pleased to grant bail to the accused-petitioners. It is further stated that till today no charge-sheet was submitted in the instant case. The Rupali Bank Limited, Foreign. Exchange Corporate Branch Motijheel, Dhaka instituted Money Suit No. 79 of 1999 in the Court of 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka, impleading one Abdul Latif, son of late Md Mokdam Ali and AFM Rafiz-uz-zaman as defendants for realizing a sum of Taka 27,34,269.63 (Taka twenty seven lakh, thirty four thousand two hundred and sixty nine and paisa sixty three) only. The aforesaid suit was decreed in ex-parte by the judgment and decree dated 27-4-2000. Thereafter the decree-holder, Rupali Bank filed Money Execution Case No. 47 of 2000 which is now pending for execution. 

 6. The Opposite-party No. 2 contested this application by filling a counter-affidavit denying the material allegations made in the application and contending, inter alia, that the Anti-Corruption Inspector, Bureau of Anti-Corruption as investigating officer upon conclusion of the investigation submitted charge-sheet being No. 414 dated 15-6-2010 under sections 406/409/467/468/471 and 109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, against 7 (seven) accused persons including the present accused-petitioners. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka on receipt of the charge-sheet on 27-7-2010 sent it to the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No. 1, Dhaka. It further appears from order No. 1 dated 16-8-2010 that the learned Judge of the Special Tribunal No. 1, Dhaka who received the case record for trial and registered it as Metro Tribunal Case No. 148 of 2010 and fixed next date on 21-10-2010 for hearing cognizance matter. Thus it is clear that the accused-petitioner by suppressing all these facts filed the present application on 22-8-2010 before the Hon'ble High Court Division under section 561A of the Code and obtained the present Rule on 25-8-2010. It is further stated that the petitioners have appropriate remedy before the Special Tribunal No. 1 Dhaka by filing an application under section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure to discharge them from the case. But the petitioners without invoking specific remedy under the Code filed this application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure which is not maintainable. Furthermore, investigation is a pre trial procedure under the Code So, the delay of investigation cannot be amount to an abuse of the process of the Court and for such reason the proceeding should not be quashed. 

 7. It further appears that when the Metro Special Tribunal Case was pending for taking cognizance before the said Tribunal, at this stage the petitioner filed this case under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the Rule and stay. The petitioner seeking quashing of the proceedings were filed before taking cognizance of the offence by the Metropolitan Special Tribunal, Dhaka. 

 8. Since the Petitioner did not come before this Hon'ble Court with clean hands, so the present application under section 561A of the Code is not maintainable and the Rule is liable to be discharged. Mr Shamsuddin Babul with Mr Ibrahim Khalil, the learned Advocates appearing for the accused petitioners, submits that there is no bar invoking section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in quashing the criminal case. Interference even at initial stage may be justified when the facts are so preposterous that even on the admitted facts no case can be started against the accused and where the institution on continuation of criminal proceedings against the accused-person may amount to an abuse of the process of the Court. 

 9. He further submits that since Money Suit No. 79 of 1999 has been decreed on the self same allegations, which is now pending for execution as such there is legal impediment to proceed with the present criminal case and the continuation of case against the accused-petitioners would amount to harassment and an abuse of the process of the Court. 

 12. After conclusion of hearing, the case was fixed for judgment on 23-6-2011, on that day, Mr Shamsuddin Bbul, the learned Advocate for the petitioners made further submissions that although the police report was submitted but the same will no way help the prosecution, since the initiations and continuation of the proceedings was void abinitio and is an abuse of the process of the Court to litigate a new case which has already been disposed of by earlier proceedings (Civil Suit) amounting to unjust harassment. In this connection learned Advocate placed reliance in the case of Hunter vs The Chief Constable of the West Midland Police reported in 1982 (AC) 529. 

 14. He further submits that the petitioners had scope and they could have raised objection, if any, before the learned Tribunal at the time of taking cognizance or framing charge under section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure or by way of revisional application before this Hon'ble Court and agitate the question raised here to correct the alleged mistake, if any. But an application under section 561A of the Code in the facts and circumstances of the case is not justified when there is an alternative remedy, 

 15. He next submits that the petitioners out of mala fide intention took resort to section 561A of the Code only to delay the disposal of the case. 

 19. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate for the Anti-Corruption Commission appearing in this case for the informant with leave of the Court has endorsed the view of the learned Assistant Attorney-General  and submits that the first information report clearly disclosed offences under sections 406/409/ 467/468/471 and 109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and after investigation police report was submitted against the accused-petitioners in the case. 

 20. He mainly submits that since the first information report clearly discloses a prima facie case against the accused-petitioners and charge-sheet was submitted on 15-6-2010. By referring order of the Special Tribunal dated 16-8-2010 submits that the accused-petitioners filed the present case before this Hon'ble Court on 22-8-2010 and Rule was issued on 25-8-2010 but the case record was transmitted by the Chief Metropolitan Court, Dhaka on 27-7-2010 and the same was received by the Senior Metropolitan Tribunal No. 1, Dhaka on 16-8-2010 and registered it as Metro Special Case No. 148 of 2010 and next date was fixed on 16-10-2010 for taking cognizance. 

 21. Since the petitioners by suppressing the aforesaid facts filed this case before taking cognizance by the competent tribunal, which is clearly a premature one as such proceeding cannot be said to be pending and the same is not liable to be quashed. On this point he relied on the latest decision of our Appellate Division reported in 60 DLR (AD) 2. 

 25. After reading of the First Information Report it appears that the FIR discloses a prima facie case against the accused-petitioners. It further appears from the charge-sheet that although in the said account no personal money through voucher was deposited or any loan was sanction or any over draft facility was given by the Branch head in the said account but two cheques were passed under the joint signatures of the petitioners, Mr Nurul Amin Chowdhury, Salah Uddin Ahmmed and another bank official. It also appears that all the seized records and document were sent to the CID to examine the specimen signature of Abdul Latif with his admitted signature appearing in his Passport. Handwriting Expert of CID, after verifying records opined that by forging the signature of Abdul Latif and in collusion of the bank officials, Taka 18,50,000 was withdrawn through two cheques and misappropriated the amount. It further appears from the police report that 'the Investigating Officer having satisfied about the prima facie case submitted charge-sheet against the accused-petitioners including other persons. In such circumstances it is very difficult to say that there were no materials to constitute any offence against the accused-petitioners. On consideration of the above materials on record, we are of the opinion that first information report discloses a prima facie case against the accused-petitioners. So we find no substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners for quashing the proceeding at this stage. 

 26. In the case of Sohail Ahmed Chowdhury vs State reported in 15 BLD 452 = 47 DLR 482; a Division Bench of this Court has held that although the inherent power of Court of the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is generally exercised for preventing an abuse of the process of the Court in respect of a pending proceeding but nevertheless the said power can also be exercised in respect of a proceeding which has reached its finality after the conclusion of the trial when it is found necessary to prevent an injustice. But this power should be exercised sparingly and in exceptional cases where the facts alleged do not constitute any criminal offence or shockingly inadequate evidence. 

 27. The jurisdiction under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is, in our opinion, of an extra ordinary nature intended to be issued in the extra-ordinary cases where there is no other remedy available. It is of a limited scope and cannot be utilized where there is other express remedy provided by the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the exercise of the inherent jurisdiction under section 561 A of the Code the High Court can neither exercise the powers of a Court of appeal nor can it enhance a sentence nor can it even reconsider question of sentence. It is design to prevent an abuse of the process of the Court and cannot be regarded as being wide enough to give to the High Court the same power that it has under section 435 read with section 439 of the Code to examine the correctness, legality and propriety and of the findings sentence or order passed by an inferior Court. Such wide power can only be exercised under section 439 of the Code. We think, therefore that the scope of jurisdiction exercised under these two provisions is not similar. These two jurisdictions are fundamentally different. These things the High Court cannot do under section 561A. Indeed, as a Rule, the inherent jurisdiction of the Court to correct an abuse of process of Court or a patent injustice cannot be invoked where there is an express provision of the Code under which the case can be adequately dealt with. 

 28. In the present case, it appears that the accused-petitioner invoked the jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code to quash the proceeding when charge-sheet was submitted before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and the offences disclosed in the charge-sheet being exclusively triable by the Special Tribunal constituted under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958, functions of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate was only to forward the same along with the charge-sheet to the Special Tribunal and no cognizance was taken against the petitioners. The petitioners against the impugned order could have moved this Court on the basis of the charge-sheet but the petitioners without taking any steps in the cognizance Court by suppressing the facts of the case moved this Court and obtained the present Rule and stay. As a matter of fact no proceeding in the proper sense as contemplated under section 561A of the Code was commenced, Such conduct of the petitioners cannot be appreciated and the petitioner without availing the alternative remedy approached this Court and obtained Rule and stay. 

 29. It has been already pointed out that the petitioners obtained Rule and stay when the case was pending before the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No. 1 Dhaka for taking cognizance. From this it should not be presumed that we are expressing the view this Court is not competent to examine propriety of the charge-sheet, but this can be done at a proper stage. It may be added that after cognizance is taken on the basis of the charge-sheet and on a proper occasion for quashing the proceedings, certainly the High Court shall examine the charge-sheet to ascertain as to whether the allegations made therein constitute a criminal offence. But before cognizance is taken by the appropriate Court, there is hardly any scope for saying that charge-sheet would lead to abuse of the process of the Court, because the Court competent to try the case has ample power to refuse taking cognizance of the offence on the facts disclosed in the police report and pass appropriate order. 

 30. Since the petitioners have failed to make out any case for our interference under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedurt4 and as such, they are not entitled to get any discretionary relief. 

 31. in a criminal case after receiving information of a cognizable offence, the police is to start investigation into such offence. As provided under section 156 of the Code the police has the statutory right to investigate into circumstances of the alleged Cognizable offence without any authority front the Magistrate and this function of the police to investigate cannot be interfered with by exercise of power under section 439 or for that matter tinder the inherent power of the Court under section 561A of the Code. 

 33. In this case, State-Opposite-party in theft' counter-affidavits filed before the High Court clearly and specifically stated that sufficient materials have been disclosed in the first information report and the charge-sheet dearly constituted a cognizable offence as provided under section 406/467/468/471 and 109 with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, and which is exclusively triable by the Special Tribunal and the same is pending before the Senior Special Tribunal No. 1 Dhaka, 

 34. Mr Shamsuddin Babul, the learned Advocate for the petitioners strenuously argued that the allegations, even if, be taken as correct, neither constitute an offence under the Penal Code nor the Prevention of Corruption Act. The learned Advocate also argued that section 561A of the Code confers unrestricted inherent power upon the High Court for the purpose of preventing abuse of the process of any Court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice. This inherent power of the High Court can be exercised in an appropriate case, even at the investigating stage when no offence any kind is disclosed and the police could have no authority to undertake an investigation. From the materials on record we find it difficult to accept the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. 

 35. This Court in a case reported in 60 DLR (AD) 1 gave further consideration to the question as to when and under what circumstances the inherent jurisdiction of the Court under section 561A of the Code may be exercised by the High Court. 

 36. It was in the case of Abdul Quader Chowdhury vs State reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38 arising out of a judgment of a Division Bench of the High Court refusing to quash the impugned proceedings in exercise of its inherent power under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure pending in the Court of Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Chittagong (North). In the present case also police submitted charge-sheet against the petitioners under sections 406/467/468/471 and 109 of the Penal Code and under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 after completing investigation on the basis of the first information report lodged by an Inspector of the Bureau of Anti-Corruption. The ease was triable by a Special Judge appointed under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958. After submission of the charge-sheet on 15-6-2010, Chief Metropolitan Magistrate transmitted the case record to the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No. 1 Dhaka on 27-7-2010 and the same was received by the Metropolitan Special judge on 16-8-2010 and was registered as Metropolitan Special Tribunal Case No. 148 of 2010. Subsequently the learned Judge of the Tribunal fixed next date on 16-10-2010 for taking cognizance hearing. At this stage the petitioners filed this application on 22-8-2010 before the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained Rule on 28-8-2010. So it will be manifestly unjust to allow the process of the Court to be issued against the accused-petitioners and continuance of the case would amount to abuse of the process of the Court and the Rule should be liable to be quashed. 

 38. Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure emphasizes that the High Court has the jurisdiction to pass orders to secure the ends of justice and for that purpose the High Court is competent to entertain applications not provided by the Code. However, it must be clearly understood that the terms of section 561A of the said Code do not extend the jurisdiction of the High Court to matters which are not inherently with that jurisdiction. The High Court also cannot claim inherent jurisdiction to exercise powers taken away by legislation. When exercising this jurisdiction, the High Court would not embark upon an enquiry whether the evidence in question is reliable or not. This is the function of the trial Magistrate and it might so happen that quashment of criminal proceedings before commencement of trial would amount to stifling the proceedings before the prosecution got an opportunity to bring evidence in support of the accusations. That is why their Lordships Judicial Committee in the case of Emperor vs. Khawaja Nazir Ahmad AIR 1945 Privy Council 18 expressed a word of caution that the Court might be acting on "treacherous grounds" in quashing criminal Proceedings at the interlocutory stage or at the early stage on the ground that continuation of the proceedings would be an abuse of the process of the Court. We fully agree with the view taken by their Lordships of the Judicial Committee that the extraordinary power of the Court under section 561A should be exercised very cautiously to avoid miscarriage of justice. 

 39. The aforesaid decision of the judicial committee of the Privy Council has been consistently followed by different superior Courts of the sub-continent including by our Appellate Division reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38 and also in a case reported in Bangladesh vs Tan Kheng Hock 31 DLR (AD) 69; Syed M Hashem vs State 48 DLR (AD) 87; N Mahmud vs N Ahmed 36 DLR (AD) 14 and latest in the case of Abdul Haque vs State 60 DLR (AD) 1. 

 40. In the case of Nazrul Islam vs State 13 MLR (AD) 185 Appellate Division held: "Quashment of proceedings at the stage before the framing of the charge is not permissible." 

 41. Mr Shamsuddin Babul, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has drawn our attention to the plaint of Money Suit No. 79 of 1999, (Annexure-C), instituted by Rupali Bank, Foreign Exchange Corporate Branch as plaintiff on 27-10-1999 impleading one Md Abdul Latif (Loanee) and AFM Rafiquzaaaman for (Guarantor) as Defendants for recovery of loan of Taka 27,34,269.63 in the 4th Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka. The said suit was decreed in ex-parte against the defendants by order dated 27-4-2000 (Annexure-C(1) and the same is now pending in Execution Case From these two Annexures it was argued by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that since the civil suit was decreed on the same self transaction, in such circumstances continuation of the present proceedings will be an abuse of the process of the Court and needs to be quashed to secure ends of justice. 

 44. In the case of Rahela Khatun vs Abul Hossain [48 DLR (AD) 213] it has been settled that: "A criminal proceeding cannot be quashed on the basis of defence materials which are still not part of the materials for the prosecution." 

 45. In this respect we may place reliance on the decision of our apex Court in the case Khandaker Abul Bashar vs State reported in 15 MLR (AD) 404 = 63 DLR (AD) 79. In paragraph 6 and 7 of the decision the Appellate Division observed that: 

 "6 There is no legal impediment to file a criminal case even if a civil suit is pending on the self-same allegations provided the ingredients of the offence are present. In the present case, the civil suit had also been dismissed for default and only a miscellaneous case for its restoration is pending. 

 47. In the present case question so far is one of investigation because, no prosecution has yet been commenced, we have not the slightest hesitation to hold that there is no reason to quash the criminal proceedings at this initial/ early stage on the ground that continuation of the present case would be an abuse of the process of the Court. We are of the view that petitioner failed to make out any case for our interference and there is no scope to quash the proceedings. 

 48. We have gone through the decisions reported in 30 DLR 237, 33 DLR 297 and 1990 BLD 110 which has been referred to us by the learned Advocate for the petitioners. All the three referred decisions relates to whether unusually long delay in commencing trial or disposal of a criminal case constitutes abuse of the process of the Court and is a ground for quashing the proceedings under section 561A of the Code. We are in the respectful agreement with the principles enunciated therein, but the facts leading to those cases are quite distinguishable with that of the instant case and as such the same have no manner of application in this particular case. Therefore, we do not find any nexus in the decision with the instant case. 

 49. In all the cited decisions proceedings was quashed after taking cognizance of the case and long delay in commencing the trial but in the case in hand petitioner before submitting police report and during investigation stage filed this case and obtained Rule and stay by suppressing the fact that after submission of charge-sheet, when the case was pending before the Special Tribunal and the same was fixed for taking cognizance. The trial is not yet stated/commenced. Thus the decisions as referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner will not any way help the petitioners. Furthermore, question of limitation does not arises in the criminal proceedings, mere delay is no ground to quash proceedings under section 561A of the Code. 

 50. A criminal prosecution is not like of civil matter, where law of limitation applies. Limitation does not apply to criminal prosecution when the state initiates prosecution for a criminal offence, such prosecution is to be deemed to have been commenced and continued in the public interest as a duty of the stage, and this is not to be lightly interfered under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Mere delay is not sufficient to establish abuse of the process of the Court. The circumstances connected with delay will have to be examined in each case to determine whether constitutes abuse of the process of the Court or not. 

 51. Admitted position in the present case is that police report was submitted on 15-6-2010 and case was fixed on 10-8-2010 for hearing cognizance matters and the present petitioner moved this Court on 28-872010 and obtained the Rule on 25-10-2010. Thus it appears that the delay in proceeding the case was due to circumstances over which prosecution had no control and for that reason proceedings cannot be quashed and such delay would not amount to abuse of the process of the Court. So, we are unable to accept the submission advanced by the learned Counsel for the petitioner. On the contrary the legal plea taken by the learned Counsel for the State-opposite-party prevails and appears to have a good deal of force. 

 55. Accordingly, the Rule is discharged. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated. The proceedings of the Motijheel Police Station Case No. 89(10)2002 corresponding to BAC GR Case No. 100 of 2002 under section 406/467/ 468/471 and 109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Anti-Corruption Act, 1947, now pending in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, shall continue in accordance with law. 

 56. Before parting with this case, it may be noted that whatever observation, we have made in judgment in connection with the disposal of this Rule and the same will have no bearing on the merit of the case in the trial. The trial Court will, however, be at liberty to have its own observation and finding of consideration of evidence that may be led by the parties in the trial.
